speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds concerning. To help me understand the nature of your symptoms, can you tell me if your double vision worsens when you look up or when you move your eyes horizontally?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest, combined with vertical diplopia, is highly suggestive of a neuromuscular junction disorder. Have you noticed any difficulty swallowing or speaking? REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_receptor_antibodies.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand your concern, but please let me confirm if you experience any ptosis (drooping eyelids) or difficulty swallowing to solidify this suspicion. DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
